claims: Colon cancer begins in the large intestine.
Colon cancer typically starts as small, noncancerous polyps that grow over time.
Colon cancer screening generally starts at age 45.
Many polyps do not produce symptoms.
Many early-stage cancers do not produce symptoms.
Colorectal cancer staging is determined by the TNM system.
TNM stands for tumor, node, metastasis.
Stage 0 colorectal cancer is carcinoma in situ.
Stage 0 colorectal cancer is localized to the inner lining.
In Stage I and II colorectal cancer, the cancer has grown into the muscle layers of the colon wall.
In Stage I and II colorectal cancer, the cancer has not spread outside the colon.
In Stage III colorectal cancer, the cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes.
Stage IV colorectal cancer is metastatic cancer.
In Stage IV colorectal cancer, the cancer has spread to distant organs like the liver or lungs.
Colon cancer risk increases particularly after age 45 or 50.
Lynch syndrome is an inherited risk factor for colon cancer.
Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is an inherited risk factor for colon cancer.
High consumption of red/processed meats is a lifestyle risk factor for colon cancer.
Lack of exercise is a lifestyle risk factor for colon cancer.
Obesity is a lifestyle risk factor for colon cancer.
Smoking is a lifestyle risk factor for colon cancer.
Excessive alcohol use is a lifestyle risk factor for colon cancer.
Colon cancer treatment includes surgery.
Colon cancer treatment includes chemotherapy.
Colon cancer treatment includes targeted therapy.
Colon cancer treatment includes immunotherapy.
The 5-year survival rate for localized cancer is around 91%.
The 5-year survival rate for cancer spread to distant parts of the body is around 15.7%.
Colon cancer symptoms include changes in bowel habits such as diarrhea, constipation, or narrowing of the stool lasting more than a few days.
Colon cancer symptoms include rectal bleeding such as bright red blood or very dark/black, tarry stool.
Colon cancer symptoms include abdominal discomfort such as persistent cramps, gas, pain, or a feeling that the bowel does not empty completely.
Colon cancer symptoms include systemic changes such as unexplained weight loss, weakness, fatigue, or anemia.
Regular screenings such as colonoscopy allow for the identification and removal of polyps before they turn into cancer.
